newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Ramos yesterday struck down a provision in the 1997 budget to ban the use of special funds for a plebiscite, fuelling opposition fears of a plot to keep him in power beyond 1998. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The military in Jolo, Sulu was placed on red alert yesterday in preparation for Thursday's burial of slain Roman Catholic Bishop Benjamin de Jesus even as police launched a manhunt for two more suspects in the February 4 gunslaying. (STAR)

- Makati-based businessmen do not want President Ramos to extend his term beyond 1998 and would rather have Defense Secretary Renato de Villa or Senator Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo as the next chief executive, according to an opinion survey of the Makati Business Club. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The country's oil refiners are inclined to turn down requests by local petroleum dealers seeking a six centavo per litre rise in prices of diesel and gasoline. (BULLETIN)

- Economic prospects for 1997 remain bullish as gross national product growth this year is expected to exceed the 6.8 percent posted last year, a recent poll conducted by the Makati Business Club among its members said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The International Monetary Fund has asked the Philippine government to consider a downward adjustment in the country's 6.5 percent inflation target for the year in view of the continuous deceleration in consumer prices, an official privy to the current consultations with the IMF said. (BUSINESS DAILY/TODAY/INQUIRER)
